## About
Kraft's Body & Fender Co is a family-owned and operated body shop on Greenlawn Ave in Columbus. Whether it's a fender bender, hail damage, a cracked windshield or a full collision, we work to get your vehicle back to its pre-accident condition.
Customers know us by name. One reviewer wrote that Bob will take the time to explain what damages have been done and what the repair process will take. Another told us the owner himself walked the few blocks to write up an estimate for the insurance company after an accident down the road.
We're rated 4.8 from 256 Google reviews. Two customers mentioned their car came back cleaned up when they picked it up. That's just how we like to hand a car back.

## Services
- Collision repair: From a shopping cart dent to a collision, we handle the body work and help minimize your downtime.
- Dent repair: Parking lot dings, door dents and shopping cart dents taken care of.
- Hail damage repair: We repair hail damage and bring the body back to its pre-accident condition.
- Bumper repair and replacement: We repair damaged bumpers or replace them when needed.
- Windshield replacement: Cracked windshield replaced here at the shop.
- Frame straightening: Frame work after a collision so your vehicle is as safe as possible for you and your family.
- Auto body painting: Custom color, pinstriping and touch-ups, with expert in-house color matching.
- Fiberglass and plastic restoration: We restore fiberglass and plastic body parts.

## FAQ
Q: Do you give free estimates?
A: Yes. Free estimates are available. Give us a call or schedule an appointment.

Q: Will you work with my insurance?
A: We accept all insurance. One reviewer said we handled communication with her insurance company, which made the whole thing less stressful.

Q: What kinds of vehicles do you work on?
A: Cars, trucks and motorcycles, foreign and domestic models.

Q: Can you match an unusual paint color?
A: We do expert in-house color matching. One customer with a unique paint color on a Camaro said we matched it spot on.
